top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a sharply defined invention: the magic-wavelength lattice removes first-order light shift and motional broadening, so many atoms can be interrogated at once and systematics rather than the atoms set the limit. It is mature, reproduced at about 1e-18 in several independent laboratories that agree in direct comparisons, and the two-person allocation matches the two clearly decisive originators, with the citation scoped to the clock itself rather than to unproven fundamental discoveries. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a solid second: a theoretical prediction followed by a clean experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect, though omitting Hasan and the 3D topological insulator work narrows the credit and it lies outside my own expertise. Either is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No direct conflict with the laureate candidates in P001 or P002. As director of WACQT and a colleague of superconducting-circuit groups I would be conflicted on circuit QED or quantum-computing proposals, but none is on this slate.
